sources_considered.why: Original research establishes language robustness problems near the claimed baseline.
Contemporary experiments examine analogy performance and sensitivity to evaluation choices.
A January 2022 research survey identifies remaining gaps in commonsense reasoning.
The original PaLM report supplies material evidence of capability improvements before the post.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Robin Jia and Percy Liang
evidence_items.explanation: The experiments establish substantial reading-comprehension brittleness near the five-year baseline. They do not measure subsequent improvement.

The study reports difficulty with abstract analogies and sensitivity to architecture and settings. This supports a limited finding of unreliable analogy performance among the tested models, not the absence of every possible solution in May 2022.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Prajjwal Bhargava and Vincent Ng
evidence_items.locator: Discussion, Exploring new components of commonsense knowledge
evidence_items.explanation: This contemporary survey identifies unaddressed commonsense capabilities and weaknesses in existing evaluations. It supports continued incompleteness but supplies no common five-year measure of reliability.
PaLM supplies material counterevidence to a reading that little capability progress occurred. These benchmark gains do not by themselves establish dependable general solutions under the contract.

unresolved_gaps: No comparable 2017–May 2022 evaluation establishes how much broad reliability changed across all four domains.
The selected studies establish particular weaknesses, not an exhaustive absence of dependable solutions.
The claim supplies no threshold separating substantial progress from 'scarcely changed'.
